title: AI Data Center Boom Ignites Bidding War for Critical TDK Unit
source_used: Japan Times (same headline and body as the Bloomberg story; no credit line visible in the extract) and TrendForce (cites Bloomberg for the bidding). Bloomberg blocked (403).
key_facts: Seagate Technology Holdings and delisted Toshiba are bidding for TDK's magnetic-heads business, which could be worth several billion dollars.
Toshiba opened talks with TDK in the spring; the bidding heated up over the summer when Seagate made a higher offer (Bloomberg, citing people familiar, via TrendForce).
TDK is the only independent supplier of magnetic recording heads and supplies Seagate, Toshiba and Western Digital (per Bloomberg, via TrendForce).
The winner could gain greater pricing power over a critical link in a highly concentrated hard-drive market; a deal would likely draw antitrust scrutiny (Bloomberg, via TrendForce).
TDK is weighing an exit from the volatile head business and could redirect resources to batteries, passive components and sensors (Bloomberg, via TrendForce).
AI data-centre demand has pushed up prices and net income at Seagate and Western Digital, which control over 90% of the global HDD market (Japan Times, citing TrendForce).
quote_evidence: Seagate Technology Holdings and delisted Toshiba are vying for TDK’s magnetic-heads business in a deal that could be worth several billion dollars.
Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, notes that Toshiba opened talks with TDK in the spring, but the bidding heated up over the summer when Seagate entered with a higher offer.
A potential deal could be worth several billion dollars, the sources said.
why_it_matters_hint: AI data centres depend on hard drives; a winning bidder could control a key supply link. Bidding not settled.
notes: Bloomberg 403 here. The Japan Times extract shows no credit line, so the Bloomberg credit rests on the identical headline and on TrendForce, which cites Bloomberg for this bidding. TrendForce (6 Oct) read for detail. Score 5 kept.
